chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has a right against another man, and he has one witness. He said, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to judge based on one witness and the oath of the owner of the right, and that is in the case of debt.'

key_terms.يَمِينُ صَاحِبِ الْحَقِّ: oath of the owner of the right (creditor)

ai.seo_question: What is the evidentiary requirement for a creditor with only one witness in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the evidentiary standard for debt claims, establishing that the Prophet (peace be upon him) accepted a single witness coupled with the creditor's oath (*yamin sahib al-haqq*) as sufficient for judgment. This ruling highlights the practical flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding financial disputes, distinguishing it from the stricter two-witness requirement often cited for other civil matters.
